lines.text: Apps are full of lists: messages, songs, scores. Today you’ll learn to walk through a list and do something with every item.
A list stores many values in order.
Each has an index (position) starting at 1.
Length tells you how many items there are.
To process every item, use an index variable i: start at 1, read item i, then change i by 1 — repeat (length of list) times.
An accumulator variable builds a result as you traverse — like adding up a total.
Starting i at 0, or forgetting to change i, are the most common list bugs.
Trace the first two loops by hand to check.
Python’s for loop traverses a list for you. The idea is exactly the same: visit every item and accumulate.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
